children: InsuranceDekho cofounders Ankit Agrawal and Ish Babbar are discussing a move to promoter roles ahead of a potential listing, even as the company says they remain in charge

IPO-bound InsuranceDekho’s cofounders are in talks to step down from their executive roles amid differences with board members over the strategic direction of the recently merged business, even as the company denies any change in their positions.

CEO Ankit Agrawal and CTO Ish Babbar are discussing a move to promoter roles while professional management takes over ahead of a potential listing, people familiar with the matter told media outlets. The development comes as the Delhi NCR-based insurtech prepares to file its draft red herring prospectus by September-end for an IPO expected by March 2027.

However, InsuranceDekho has rubbished the reports. “The cofounders remain actively involved with InsuranceDekho and continue to lead the company’s strategy and growth alongside the broader leadership team. There has been no change in their roles or their commitment to the company,” a company spokesperson said.

The startup is aiming to go public by March 2027. Its IPO is likely to be worth around Rs 3,000-4,000 crore, with the startup seeking a valuation of around Rs 9,500 crore. The IPO is expected to comprise both a fresh issue of equity shares and an offer for sale by existing investors. The fresh issue would likely constitute a larger portion of the IPO size, though the structure will be finalised closer to the listing.

Delhi NCR-based InsuranceDekho was founded as the insurance arm of used car marketplace CarDekho in 2016 by Agrawal and Babbar. It was later hived off as a separate business. The startup offers motor, health, life and other insurance products. It has also been granted a composite broking licence from the regulator, allowing it to offer reinsurance services. Besides, it operates Heph, a SaaS platform for insurance distributors.
To date, it has raised USD 430 million from the likes of Avataar Venture Partners, TVS Capital Funds, Goldman Sachs, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group and insurer BNP Paribas Cardif.

InsuranceDekho recently announced the completion of its merger with rival insurance distributor RenewBuy after the Competition Commission of India gave the green light to the deal last November. The combined entity, operating under InsuranceDekho’s brand, is being led by Agrawal with RenewBuy’s founders remaining on board. It now claims to be India’s largest AI-enabled insurance distribution platform in terms of the insurance premium generated through point-of-sales persons in FY26.

The combined entity now operates as an open, multi-insurer ecosystem, enabling choice across motor, health, life and commercial insurance, backed by integrated digital onboarding, policy issuance and AI-powered advisory. In a statement on September 1, the startup said that the founders of both InsuranceDekho and RenewBuy will continue in the merged organisation, “ensuring continuity in leadership, execution and long-term strategy”.
Post the merger, InsuranceDekho claims its premium book is worth over Rs 6,600 crore and it offers more than 750 insurance products through partnerships with 52 insurers.
